extracted.intended_audience: applicant institutions, training PD/PIs, fellowship sponsors/administrators, and prospective Kirschstein-NRSA fellows
extracted.subtask_description: Terms, conditions, allowable costs, reporting, and eligibility rules for individual Kirschstein-NRSA fellowships and institutional research training grants (NRSA/T32 and related mechanisms). Includes stipend/tuition/benefit rules, supplementation/compensation rules, reporting and change-of-project procedures, and program eligibility requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tuition and fees for postdoctoral and senior fellowships
rubrics_metrics.description: For individual postdoctoral fellowships (F32) and individual senior fellowships (F33), an amount equal to 60% of the actual tuition level at the applicant institution, up to $4,500 per year, will be provided. If the fellow is enrolled in a program that supports postdoctoral individuals in formal degree-granting training, the amount provided will be 60% of the actual tuition level, up to $16,000 per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For postdoctoral fellows, costs associated with tuition and fees are allowable only if they are required for specific courses in support of the research training. Health insurance is not included in this budget item because costs for it are to be charged as institutional allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health insurance charged to institutional allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Health insurance costs for NRSA fellowships are to be charged as institutional allowance rather than as tuition/fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is now consistent with treatment of health insurance for postdoctoral fellowships; health insurance should not be included in the tuition budget item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel to foreign training sites
rubrics_metrics.description: For fellows at foreign training sites, awards may include a single economy or coach round-trip travel fare in addition to the institutional allowance; no allowance for dependents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: U.S. flag air carriers must be used to the maximum extent possible for travel between U.S. and foreign countries or between foreign countries. Any funds awarded for travel to/from foreign training sites must be reported on the Termination Notice as part of the 'Amount of Stipend' column. See Cost Considerations for additional foreign travel guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Childcare costs (allowability and conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Childcare costs are allowable for full-time NRSA fellows and full-time recipients of Predoctoral to Postdoctoral Fellow Transition Award (F99/K00) programs during the F99 phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Childcare must be provided by a licensed childcare provider; recipients must maintain supporting documentation (e.g., proof provider is licensed) and make it available to NIH upon request (not routinely submitted). Childcare costs are not tied to payback obligations, generally restricted and cannot be re-budgeted without prior written approval from the NIH awarding IC, and unused portions on early termination remain unobligated and will be adjusted in closeout. Cost levels are updated periodically and published in the NIH Guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee benefits not chargeable to fellowships
rubrics_metrics.description: Because Kirschstein-NRSA fellowships are not a condition of employment, institutions may not seek funds or charge fellowship awards for costs normally associated with employee benefits (e.g., FICA, workman's compensation, life insurance, union dues, unemployment insurance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a fellow requests that the institution deduct certain personal costs (e.g., union dues) from the stipend, the institution can provide such a service only with approval of the fellow; deductions cannot be automatic without fellow's approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebudgeting restrictions for individual fellowships
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual fellowship awards are formula based, generally restricted for specific budget categories of the award, and cannot be rebudgeted without prior written approval from the NIH awarding IC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stipends must be expended using the stipend level provided and cannot be rebudgeted into stipend to accommodate a different stipend level. Unexpended stipends on early termination must be returned and cannot be rebudgeted. Institutional allowance is a fixed amount with allowable costs; if unexpended, it can only be rebudgeted into tuition and fees when tuition and fees have been awarded. Tuition and fees, when awarded, are generally restricted and cannot be rebudgeted without prior written approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipend supplementation (non‑Federal funds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stipends may be supplemented by an institution from non‑Federal funds provided this supplementation is without any additional obligation for the fellow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions determine supplementation amounts per their formal policies, which must be consistently applied to all individuals in similar status regardless of funding source. Federal funds (including PHS funds) may not be used for stipend supplementation unless specifically authorized by the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation and part‑time employment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows may seek part‑time employment incidental to training; fellows and trainees may spend on average an additional 25% of their time (e.g., ~10 hours/week) in part‑time research, teaching, or clinical employment, so long as those activities do not interfere with or lengthen the NRSA training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funds characterized as compensation may be paid only when there is an employer‑employee relationship, payments are for services rendered, and conditions for compensation of students (per Cost Considerations) are met. Compensation must follow organizational policies applied consistently across federally and non‑federally supported activities and be supported by acceptable accounting records. Compensation may not be paid from a research grant that supports the same research that is part of the fellow’s approved training experience. Sponsors must approve employment on research grants to verify it will not detract from or prolong training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent awards and other income restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: A Kirschstein‑NRSA individual fellowship may not be held concurrently with another federally sponsored fellowship or similar Federal or non‑Federal award that provides a stipend or otherwise duplicates provisions of the Kirschstein‑NRSA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An individual may accept educational remuneration from the VA (GI Bill) and Federal educational loan funds concurrently; such funds are not considered supplementation or compensation. Postdoctoral fellows may be eligible for NIH Loan Repayment Program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxability of stipends
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 117 of the Internal Revenue Code applies to tax treatment of scholarships and fellowships. Degree candidates may exclude from gross income amounts used for qualified tuition and related expenses; non‑degree candidates generally must report monies paid on their behalf as gross income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH does not provide tax advice and takes no position on individual taxpayer status; individuals should consult IRS. The IRS regulations (Revenue Procedures 2005‑11) do not, per NIH, apply to or impact Kirschstein‑NRSA programs or awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 1099 reporting practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Although stipends are not considered salaries, they are subject to Federal and sometimes State income tax and may be reported by the sponsoring institution on IRS Form 1099.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsoring institutions (domestic non‑Federal) normally prepare and issue Form 1099 for fellows paid through the institution but are not required to do so. Fellows must still report stipends even if Form 1099 is not issued. For fellows training at a Federal or foreign laboratory and receiving stipend from NIH, PMS will issue a Form 1099.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activation Notice reporting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals must complete and sign the Ruth L. Kirschstein Individual Fellowship Activation Notice (Form PHS 416‑5) upon initiation of training, obtain AOR signature, and forward it with the Payback Agreement (if required) to the NIH awarding IC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activation may be on or after the NoA issue date up to the latest activation date (generally 6 months). For fellows paid directly by PMS (foreign/Federal sponsors) Activation Notice required for initial year only and should be submitted immediately prior to initiation of training. Activation Notice may be submitted up to 30 days before start for payroll purposes, but funds must not be released until training begins. Competing continuations must be activated on the day following prior award's budget period end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payback Agreement requirement (postdocs)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Ruth L. Kirschstein NRSA Payback Agreement (Form PHS 6031) covering the initial 12 months of postdoctoral NRSA support must be signed by each person receiving an individual postdoctoral fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not required if the individual has already received 12 months of postdoctoral NRSA support under any NRSA institutional or fellowship award. No Payback Agreement required for predoctoral fellows. See Payback Reporting Requirements for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination Notice requirement and timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRSA Termination Notice (Form PHS 416‑7) is the basis for validating total NRSA support period and establishing payback amount; for individual fellowships it must be submitted within 30 days of the termination date even if fellow is not available for signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information is usually verified by sponsor and an institutional business official; if sponsor unavailable, institutional business official may verify. Lack of timely/accurate information may adversely affect aggregate NRSA support data and payback. For foreign training site awards, travel funds must be reported on Termination Notice in 'Amount of Stipend' column. All Termination Notices for individual fellowships must be submitted electronically using eRA Commons xTrain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consecutive support and payback deferral
rubrics_metrics.description: If a fellow switches NRSA mechanisms (e.g., institutional training grant to individual fellowship) or NIH ICs, payback service requirement is deferred until the total period of NRSA support is completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All fellowship applications are reviewed to determine prior NRSA support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progress reporting (RPPR and IDP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual progress reports (Research Performance Progress Report, RPPR) are required for non‑competing continuation support of fellowships; the IDP requirement applies to individual fellowships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inadequate or incomplete progress reports may delay continued support. Final progress report information is required as part of the Termination Notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial reporting exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: An annual or final FFR to report expenditure information is not required for NRSA individual fellowship awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfers, sponsor change, and project change approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval of the NIH awarding IC is required for transfer of an award to another institution, a change in sponsor, or a project change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a fellow sponsored by a domestic non‑Federal institution requests transfer to another domestic non‑Federal institution before end of current award year, institutions negotiate which will pay stipend until year end and disposition of institutional allowance. No Activation Notice is required from the new sponsoring organization; appointment remains active in xTrain. Transfers involving Federal or foreign sponsors require unique procedures and should be discussed with the awarding IC. Any proposed change in specified area of research training must be reviewed and approved in writing by the awarding IC to ensure training remains within original peer‑reviewed scope. If sponsor will be absent >3 months, an interim sponsor must be named and approved in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leave policies (vacation, sick, parental, terminal, unpaid)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows may receive the same vacations and holidays as comparable trainees and continue to receive stipends during those times. Sick leave up to 15 calendar days per year with possible extension by awarding IC; parental leave up to 60 calendar days (8 work weeks) per year for adoption or birth of each child, requiring advanced notification and sponsor approval. Terminal leave is not permitted. Unpaid leave beyond sick/parental limits requires NIH approval and will extend project end date; award funds cannot be spent during unpaid leave though health insurance coverage may continue per institutional policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation to suspend award and/or accrual of payback service must be completed and retained during leave; leave must be documented on Termination Notice when fellowship ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination for noncompliance or request
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH may terminate an NRSA individual fellowship early if the recipient materially failed to comply with terms or failed to carry out award purpose; NIH will notify fellow in writing with reasons and appeal rights. NIH may also terminate at the request of sponsoring institution or fellow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fellow receives another NIH award making them PD/PI (e.g., R03), they are no longer eligible for the fellowship and sponsor should contact awarding IC regarding early termination. On early termination, stipend must be prorated; if final budget period was 6 months or less, at least one‑half of institutional allowance must be refunded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publications and sharing of research results
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients should make results and accomplishments available to the research community and public; no restrictions should be placed on publication of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows are encouraged to submit findings to journals of their choice. Responsibility for project direction should not be ascribed to NIH. NIH support must be acknowledged by footnote using specified language and Public Access Policy requirements apply to articles authored/co‑authored by NRSA fellows that arose from NIH support. Information on publications is included in annual progress report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright policy
rubrics_metrics.description: When a publication or copyrightable material is developed from NIH‑supported work, the author is free to arrange for copyright without NIH awarding IC approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any copyrighted materials shall be subject to a royalty‑free, nonexclusive, irrevocable right to the Federal agency to reproduce, publish, and otherwise use the work for Federal purposes and to authorize others to do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventions and patents (exception for NIH training)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships funded primarily for educational purposes are not subject to invention reporting requirements and NIH has no rights to inventions under those awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: Kirschstein‑NRSA fellows training at NIH are subject to EO 10096 provisions and NIH determines disposition of rights to any invention conceived or first actually reduced to practice during the fellowship period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of professional fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees from clinical practice, professional consultation, or comparable activities performed pursuant to award must be assigned to the sponsoring institution for disposition per organizational policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'professional fees' does not apply to honoraria, fees for scholarly writing, occasional outside lectures, or advisory service to public/non‑profit organizations, which, if allowed by organizational policy, may be retained by the fellow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public policy requirements applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: All Public Policy Requirements, Objectives, and Appropriation Mandates discussed in Part IIA apply to individual NRSA fellowships when appropriate (e.g., civil rights, human subjects protections, inclusion policies, humane care and use of animals, human embryonic stem cells, synthetic nucleic acid research).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsoring institution is responsible for ensuring fellow has proper training/education and supervision, particularly for human subjects, vertebrate animal research, and occupational safety programs. See IIA and Individual Fellowship Application Guide for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of NIH Standard Terms of Award (exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual Fellowships are awarded under the NIH Standard Terms of Award; however, provisions to extend the final budget period of a project period without additional funds and carryover of unobligated balances do not apply to fellowships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and scope of institutional research training grants
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH will award Kirschstein‑NRSA institutional research training grants to eligible institutions to develop or enhance research training opportunities selected by the institution for individuals training for research careers in biomedical, behavioral, and clinical research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training can be in basic biomedical or clinical sciences, behavioral or social sciences, health services research, or other disciplines relevant to NIH mission. Program supports predoctoral, postdoctoral, and short‑term training and limited pre‑baccalaureate support. Most NIH ICs award these grants; FIC and NLM have separate authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility for institutional training grants
rubrics_metrics.description: A domestic, non‑profit public or private organization may apply for a grant to support a research training program in specified research area(s); support for predoctoral, postdoctoral, or combination of trainees may be requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific program announcements may have IC guidelines. Applications must use research training forms and instructions; short‑term training for health‑professional students may be requested where indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research area alignment with NIH IC mission
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional training grants may be made for training in areas that fall within the missions of the NIH ICs; applications not addressing these areas will be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is increased emphasis on physician research training; HHS Secretary must give special consideration to physicians undertaking >=2 consecutive years of research training. Applicant institution must have strong research program, staff and facilities to carry out proposed program. Trainees must have opportunity for supervised research aimed at developing research skills for a research career.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training PD/PI qualifications and leadership for multiple PD/PIs
rubrics_metrics.description: The Training PD/PI must have skills, knowledge, and resources to organize and implement a high‑quality research training program and is responsible for trainee selection, overall direction, management, program evaluation, and timely submission of required forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple PD/PIs are allowed for team approaches; applications with multiple PD/PIs require a Leadership Plan emphasizing benefits to the training program and trainees and describe structure/governance. Multiple PD/PIs share authority and responsibility; a single Contact PD/PI must be designated for NIH communication. NIH will not allocate budget or positions between PD/PIs and only a single award is issued. Multiple PD/PIs should be reasonable in number and each included for a specific purpose; do not list all mentors as PD/PIs except in unusual cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use restrictions for institutional training grants and full‑time requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An institutional training grant must support a program of research training and may not support studies leading to clinical/professional degrees (M.D., D.D.S., D.V.M., etc.) except as part of a formal combined research degree program (e.g., M.D./Ph.D.). Trainees are expected to devote full time to proposed research training (generally defined as at least 40 hours/week or institutional policy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clinicians may engage in full‑time postdoctoral research training even when that experience counts toward clinical board certification. To meet full‑time requirement, clinicians must confine clinical duties to those integral to research training experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predoctoral degree eligibility rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Predoctoral research training is for individuals with a baccalaureate (or equivalent) enrolled postbaccalaureate in programs leading to a Ph.D. or comparable research doctoral degree or combined clinical degree and Ph.D. Individuals who already hold specified doctoral degrees (Ph.D., M.D., D.D.S., etc.) are not eligible for predoctoral training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students in integrated dual‑degree programs (e.g., M.D./Ph.D.) maintain predoctoral status while enrolled concurrently, even if the professional degree is awarded before the research doctorate. A student cannot possess both predoctoral and postdoctoral statuses. Students in separate, non‑integrated dual degree paths lose predoctoral status if one degree is completed before the other. Students in health‑professional programs who postpone professional studies to gain research experience may be appointed; predoctoral training must emphasize fundamental training in basic biomedical, behavioral, and clinical sciences.
